articleTitle: Local Path Planning for AGV Based on a Mathematical Model of Envelope
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The generation of motion paths of Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) is a critical aspect of logistics and unmanned factory production systems. Currently, researchers mainly enhance path smoothness in AGV local path planning by employing optimization techniques such as Bezier curves and B-spline curves. However, these methods often require high-standard site conditions or involve complex computations. This paper establishes a mathematical model for AGV curved path segments and its envelope lines of motion using polynomial curves with better comprehensive properties. The study combines theoretical analysis with experimental validation, demonstrating advantages such as smoother path generation, smaller turning radii, and simpler computational methods. In addition, parameters with better properties are selected to verify the correctness and feasibility of polynomial curves as motion control curves for AGV turning, providing a theoretical basis for active obstacle avoidance in AGV operations.

articleTitle: A method for real-time compensation of nonlinear error in Rotary Tool Center Point mode
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is presented for real-time compensation of nonlinear error in the Rotary Tool Center Point (RTCP) mode on five-axis Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machines. Despite the advantages of RTCP in reducing errors, they persist between interpolation points. The tool model and its temporal state description are defined in this paper, elucidates the principles and calculation methods for the generation of nonlinear error during the machining process, and proposes a method to further reduce nonlinear error in RTCP mode based on the kinematic modeling of dual rotary table machines. This method takes the direction and magnitude of error compensation as two dimensions, using the bilateral coefficient method to calculate the error compensation direction at each interpolation point based on the actual error size, and employs the root mean square roughness as an indirect indicator to measure the magnitude of nonlinear error, calculating the size of error compensation. By dividing the global optimization into optimization per single interpolation period, the method allows for the calculation and acquisition of the actual target position value of the current interpolation point after compensation within each interpolation period, providing a reference for real-time prediction and compensation.

articleTitle: FRNet: A Full-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network for OCTA Vascular Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) is an advanced, non-invasive imaging technique. Automatic segmentation of vascular networks in retinal OCTA images is essential for the early diagnosis and progression assessment of various vision-related diseases. However, most existing methods for OCTA image vessel segmentation rely on encoder-decoder architectures, which typically involve a high number of parameters and result in slower inference speeds. In this paper, we introduce FRNet V2, an accurate and efficient neural network specifically designed for retinal vessel segmentation in OCTA images. This is achieved by integrating a modified recursive ConvNeXt V2 block and a recursive HAAM attention mechanism into a full-resolution convolutional network framework. We evaluate our proposed method on two large public datasets: ROSSA and OCTA-500. Experimental results demonstrate that our network achieves performance on par with other methods, while boasting significantly fewer parameters and faster inference speeds. This makes it highly suitable for practical industrial applications.

articleTitle: Efficient template-based robotic sorting with one-shot multi-object pose estimation algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In industrial sorting, the efficiency and accuracy of robotic systems are crucial for optimizing manufacturing and logistics processes. Traditional template-based methods such as point pair feature (PPF) and iterative closest point (ICP) are widely used to obtain robust pose estimation solutions. However, in practice, their efficiency is highly dependent on the templates of workpieces. In this paper, we developed an efficient robotic sorting system with a template-based pose estimation algorithm for static sorting tasks. Considering the redundancy of the nominal template, we optimized the template by sparsifying its point clouds and cutting the hidden part. The proposed algorithm can achieve a one-shot multi-object pose estimation functionality, which includes point cloud segmentation, cluster, and registration. The random sample consensus (RANSAC) is used to segment the point clouds of workpieces from the background. The principal component analysis (PCA) is used to distinguish object categories. The PPF and ICP are used to achieve the coarse and fine registration, respectively. We conducted 60 groups of experiments to compare the optimized template with the nominal template. The experimental results showed that the average time taken by the optimized template to register the wheel and cube workpieces was 5.78 s and 7.73 s, respectively. However, the average time to register with the nominal template was 105.18 s and 191.09 s, respectively. The proposed method can generally achieve a 20-time efficiency improvement and a good performance in actual sorting experiments.

articleTitle: Mechanism Design of Cable-driven Multi-functional Knee Osteoarthritis Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis is a chronic degenerative disease commonly seen in middle-aged and elderly people. At present, the number of patients with knee osteoarthritis is increasing year by year, accounting for 21.51% of the total patients. Today, knee osteoarthritis rehabilitation robots have made breakthrough progress, but safety and portability are still the key issues to be solved, and further research and improvement are needed to achieve a wider application. By studying the functions of common lower limb rehabilitation robots and the rehabilitation needs of patients with knee osteoarthritis, this paper proposes design requirements and schemes. It conducts dynamic and kinematic analysis, and establishes three-dimensional models. The goal is to complete the mechanism design of wearable knee osteoarthritis rehabilitation robots, aiming to enhance the effectiveness and overall performance of the rehabilitation robots. The main feature of this design is the use of cable driver module design and varus and valgus knee orthoses mechanism design, which can help the knee dysfunction patients to provide stable support and efficiently complete rehabilitation training.

articleTitle: Intelligent mower path planning based on improved A* algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: With the continuous focus on environmental issues, the greening of the grassland has also received attention, and the demand for the automated maintenance of the grassland is also escalating. Therefore, the intelligent mower is playing an increasingly crucial role. This paper addresses the issue of the working path planning of the mower based on the improvement of the A* algorithm. After obtaining the working map, obstacle expansion processing is initially conducted to avert collisions, then the area is divided and the path is pre-planned in a serpentine, and finally, the improved A* algorithm is employed to connect the paths at the beginning and end of each area. Additionally, path optimization has been made for the actual requirements to strengthen the operating reliability and stability. And the DWA algorithm is introduced to achieve dynamic obstacle avoidance and to enhance the versatility and safety of the mower. Finally, the experiment verified the feasibility and reliability of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel multi-source domain transfer learning method for remaining useful life prediction using multi-scale attention-based temporal convolutional network
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Transfer learning methods have found extensive applications in the prognostics and health management (PHM) field, greatly improving model generalization across multiple operational scenarios. However, current transfer learning methods for predicting remaining useful life (RUL) rely on single-source domain adaptation strategies, which do not fully exploit information from multiple source domains. To address this issue, a novel method for multi-source domain transfer learning is proposed, aimed at predicting RUL under variable conditions. A multi-scale attention based temporal convolutional network is designed for domain feature extraction. Domain adversarial learning and domain distribution alignment strategies are introduced to reduce distribution discrepancies between the source and target domains. The approach leverages multi-source domain adaptation to achieve effective knowledge transfer from multiple source domains, thereby improving prediction accuracy in the target domain. Experimental results validated the efficacy of the proposed method, demonstrating that its performance surpasses that of existing approaches.

articleTitle: 2D-LLFE-NVC: 2D Laser Line Feature Extraction Using Normal Vector Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel 2D laser data line feature extraction algorithm based on normal vector clustering(2D-LLFE-NVC). The algorithm consists of normal vector calculation, normal normalization based on multi-scale operator normal difference and median filter, and line feature extraction based on normal vector clustering. Unlike existing methods, 2D-LLFE-NVC leverages the continuity of laser point clouds and detects breakpoints using multi-scale operators based on normal differences. The extracted line features are more accurate and correct on a global scale. To validate its performance, we conducted SLAM experiments in a 5000-square-meter indoor environment using both the proposed algorithm and existing methods. By comparing the line feature points extracted by these different approaches with manually annotated line feature points, and demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of correctness and completeness.

articleTitle: Development of A Three-state Clamper for Multi-joint Sequence-driven Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Assisted exoskeleton robots are gradually being used in industrial production in order to reduce the risk of workers suffering from work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). To lower the weight of the exoskeleton and improve its applicability, the active degrees of freedom of exoskeletons are often reduced in prototype designs. However, this may decrease the exoskeleton's output power and working capacity. To address this, we propose a tendon-sheath-based multi-joint actuation method that uses a single motor to sequentially drive multiple degrees of freedom, and applies it to the design of the shoulder and elbow joints of the upper limb exoskeleton. To do this, we develop a clamper remotely controlled by a steering gear, which has three working modes and is used to switch the position of the end anchor point of the tendon sheath artificial muscle. The clamper can clamp wire ropes with diameters of 1-2 mm and provide a maximum clamping force of 800 N. The performance of the multi-joint exoskeleton and the clamper was tested by experiments. The results show that the clamper can quickly control the tendon sheath artificial muscle to achieve the sequential movement of the multiple joints, and it only takes about 100ms to 150ms to switch between the three working modes.

articleTitle: A Study of Open-Source Leaf Instance Segmentation Approaches Against Diverse Leaf Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In the quest for sustainable agriculture and accurate yield prediction, deep learning approaches are utilized for leaf segmentation to automate and enhance quantifying plant characteristics, contributing to efficient agricultural practices. This study compares three deep learning leaf segmentation methods: a bottom-up instance segmentation method, a Segment Anything Model (SAM) with post-processing, and a fine-tuned Mask R-CNN. Their performance is evaluated using standard metrics on three datasets: the CVPPP Leaf Segmentation Challenge, Komatsuna, and Michigan State University Dense Leaves. The fine-tuned Mask R-CNN achieves the highest precision and dice scores, indicating superior performance. The SAM approach demonstrates the potential for zero-shot leaf segmentation, while the bottom-up method struggles with accurate leaf delineation. Exploring efficient tuning techniques and lightweight models is recommended to enhance performance while reducing computational demands.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Facial Expression Recognition Method Based on Multi-task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Facial expression recognition remains a prominent research area in computer vision, particularly due to its significant contributions in the field of human emotion analysis. However, the effectiveness of current deep learning approaches in representing facial expressions faces considerable hurdles stemming from ambiguities in dataset annotations, which notably impact recognition accuracy. In response, this paper introduces a multi-task facial expression recognition network (MTFERN) that integrates Adaptive Feature Fusion Module (AFFM) and Distribution Consistent Attention Pooling Module (DCAPM). The purpose of these modules is to tackle the difficulties caused by annotation ambiguities through the inclusion of auxiliary branches. These branches analyze the distribution of labels within samples and compute attention weights accordingly, enhancing the network’s ability to discern subtle variations in facial expressions. Experimental evaluations conducted on benchmark datasets such as FER2013 and AffectNet show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed expression recognition algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and Preliminary Evaluation of a Serial-Parallel Hybrid Robot for Cataract Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis (CCC) is a delicate operation that may benefit from robot technology. This paper introduces a new hybrid cataract surgery robot that consists of four parallel prismatic pairs connected in series to a "Rotation-Prismatic" unit. Additionally, the paper proposes a master-slave control strategy and a virtual remote center of motion (RCM) algorithm. The virtual RCM is based on the kinematic model of the robot and enables the setting of an arbitrary point on the forceps as the RCM point. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed robot is verified through experimental evaluations on ex-vivo pig eyeballs.

articleTitle: Development of a PLCopen-Based Controller for Flexible Fatigue Test Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Aiming at the flexibility and reconfigurability needs for fatigue test applications, the demand for a PLCopen-based development framework arises. In this study, we utilize the IEC 61131-3 programmable language and PLCopen specifications to design the controller for electro-hydraulic servo loading system. Firstly, PLCopen group function block diagrams are proposed in accordance with experiments. Multiple groups can manage different experiments simultaneously. Then, PLCopen channel function block diagrams are designed to manage district channels in a group. To correct tracking errors, each channel incorporates a peak-valley phase compensator. Peak-valley phase compensator could potentially be used to adjust for multi-frequency sinusoidal spectrum. Finally, simulation and experiment results verify that tracking error could be kept within a defined neighbourhood region.

articleTitle: Grasp Detection Method Based on Grasp Center and Key Features
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: There is a problem in the field of grasp detection that the grasp center and key features are not prominent, to handle this, a new strategy for giving the grasping quality score within the grasping rectangle is proposed, and the grasping key features is extracted with the help of the attention mechanism in this paper. We introduce CBAM, which is a hybrid of channel attention and spatial attention, into the GR-CNN, to make the network more attentive to key information, and reduces the number of its channels to reduce the number of parameters. The network outputs predicted grasping positions and scores with the grasping center position closer to the center of the object and better estimates of width and angle. Experiments are conducted on the Cornell and Jacquard datasets with accuracies of 97.8% and 93.5%, respectively. The experiments show that proposed method has good performance.

articleTitle: Research on emotional recognition methods based on electrocardiogram signal
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: A sentiment electrocardiogram dataset was constructed through emotional reproduction experiments. By screening the signals and eliminating abnormal waveform signals, 38 groups of high-quality emotional ECG data were obtained for each emotional state, and the construction of effective data sets was completed. Through random forest (RF) classification research, support vector machine (SVM) and K-nearest neighbor (KNN) validation are used to construct an effective emotion recognition model, and the outstanding ability of RF algorithm in emotion recognition is verified. Specifically, the average recognition rate reached RF (93.8%), 5NN (90.525%), 7NN (91.375%), 9NN (92.0253%) and SVM (90.775%). The confusion matrix and F1 score evaluation of recognition model and validation model show the superior performance of RF model for emotion recognition, the effectiveness of the system and the rationality of the feature analysis method are demonstrated.

Index Terms: Performance Of The Random Forest Model

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Series Elastic Actuator Based on Parallel Springs
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: This paper proposes a Series Elastic Actuator aimed at reducing the impact forces on joints during specific movements to prevent damage to the mechanical structure from excessive external forces during machine operation. The SEA uses a planar structure with input and output terminals coupled through a spring, featuring a compact axial design. The output torque is modeled based on the actuator's dynamics to determine the torque-deflection relationship. The accuracy of the torque estimation model is studied by comparing the estimated torque with the torque measured by a torque sensor. The model's estimated RMSE value is 0.3302 Nm, the maximum error is 0.9837 Nm, and the standard deviation is 0.1990 Nm. The results indicate that the model can effectively estimate the output torque of the proposed SEA. Additionally, the actuator's open-loop frequency response was tested to study its response to input signals of different frequencies. The open-loop amplitude response and phase response graphs of the system were plotted, showing that the system's amplitude attenuated to -3 dB at an input signal frequency of 1.67 Hz, and the reasons for this phenomenon were analyzed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Digital Twin Machine Tool Interface Layout Based on Situation Awareness
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The digital twin technology of CNC machine tools is widely used in the manufacturing industry, and a reasonable information layout is crucial for improving the situational awareness and work efficiency of operators. Therefore, using scientific methods to evaluate and analyze different information layout schemes plays an important auxiliary role in interface design. This paper takes the digital twin machine interface as a case study to evaluate the situational awareness level of its interface layout. Firstly, an evaluation system for the level of situational awareness of interface layout was constructed, and the weights of each indicator were calculated using the Analytic Hierarchy Process. Secondly, taking eight different layout schemes as examples, analyze and evaluate each design scheme using the interface layout situational awareness evaluation criteria. Finally, compare and verify the results, and evaluate and rank the comprehensive situational awareness level. The experimental results help designers choose more efficient and situational awareness interface design solutions in practice, providing certain reference value for other interface research.

articleTitle: Molobicus Tilapia Measurement Using Computer Vision and Polynomial Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The post-harvest sector of the aquaculture industry in the Philippines potentially lose profits due to the lack of an accurate system for measuring Molobicus Tilapia fish length. In this paper, computer vision was used as a non-invasive tool to measure the fish length. Polynomial regression spanning from 1st to 5th order were used and compared to trace the fish’s body line. Using three different images of a same fish, each polynomial order were evaluated and compared to the manual measurement. Results show that lower ordered polynomial curve fits were more accurate and precise with errors averaging at 2.45%.

articleTitle: An AGV Scheduling Problem Based on Partial Charging Policy
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) have become common devices in intelligent manufacturing environments. This paper studies a scheduling problem for AGVs, in which a fleet of homogeneous AGVs are used to deliver parts to workstations in a shop floor environment. Due to the limited battery capacity of the AGV, we have adopted a partial charging policy in this paper. The transportation tasks undertaken by each AGV and the charging operations on each AGV need to be scheduled. The objective is to minimize the makespan to complete all transportation tasks. A mixed integer programming model is presented to describe the AGV scheduling problem. A two-stage heuristic approach is proposed for problem-solving. For stage one, a hybrid genetic whale optimization algorithm (HGWOA) is developed to assign transportation tasks to each AGV. For stage two, a rule-based heuristic is proposed to schedule the assigned transportation tasks and charging operations for each AGV. Computational experiments show that the proposed solution procedures can solve the scheduling problem effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: A Study on User's Cognitive Needs in Virtual Reality Training Systems from an Embodied Cognition Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) technology has been successfully applied to training and learning across multiple fields, significantly enhancing user training outcomes and experience. However, current research on virtual equipment training platforms primarily focuses on virtual assembly, algorithm optimization, and collision detection, with little emphasis on user experience and immersion. Therefore, this paper explores the cognitive needs of users in VR-based training environments from the perspective of embodied cognition. Through Think-aloud experiments, user research, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), combined with insights from embodied cognition theory, the primary factors affecting user cognition in virtual reality equipment training are identified. These factors can provide guidance for the design of future VR training systems, ensuring they are more aligned with natural learning processes and user interactions, ultimately leading to improved user satisfaction, deeper knowledge retention, and more effective training outcomes.

articleTitle: Design of a Compliant Microgripper by Combining a Voice Coil Motor and a Monolithic Modular Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In this paper, a new compliant microgripper integrating a voice coil motor and a monolithic modular mechanism is designed, analyzed, and studied by simulation. It adopts the modularization idea to divide the overall mechanism into five functional sections. The purpose of the mechanism design is to convert the output displacement of the motor into the gripping motion of two jaws. Compound parallelogram flexures and compound radial flexures are the core elements that enable linear transmission and directional change of motion. The flexible seesaw mechanism allows the gripper to continue to work even if one side of the jaws is blocked. The gripper has a bi-directional large stroke output, which enables both a normally open operation and a normally closed operation. The output stroke of the motor is restricted to prevent excessive deformation and damage to the target arising from displacement overshoot. Theoretical models are derived to obtain critical structural parameters that affect the performance of the gripper. Simulation results indicate that the gripper has good static and dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Pupil localization based on dual edges and occlusion compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Gaze-based interaction technology has been prompted in response to the problem of interaction obstacles of some people caused by the limitations of keyboard and mouse control in the current human-computer interaction. The key step in the vision tracking technology, the pupil, has the problem of low accuracy of pupil center positioning due to the occlusion of the eyelid in the image and the reflection of part of the light, which seriously affects the effect of the human-computer interaction technology based on vision tracking. Therefore, this paper proposes a pupil localization algorithm based on dual edges and occlusion compensation. Firstly, preprocessing such as Gaussian blur is applied to the eye image. Then, histogram-based thresholding is used to binarize the image, obtaining binary image edges and eye image edges. Pupil contour extraction is performed based on dual edges, followed by ellipse fitting using the least squares method to obtain pupil information. Taking into account the problem of poor pupil localization under occlusion, this paper also presents a method to acquire effective edge information and compensate contour points to enhance the accuracy of localization. The experimental results demonstrate that the method proposed in this paper achieves an accuracy of 70.85% on the public dataset LPW, which is 2% higher than the LVCF method. Furthermore, it can effectively locate the pupils under various occlusion conditions.

articleTitle: Forecasting Taiwan's International Trade: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Approach for Extracting Economic Cycle Indicators
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: International trade correlates positively with global economic development. Recent disruptions, such as the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent logistical challenges, have highlighted the importance of accurate trade predictions for assessing economic recovery. However, forecasting trade remains challenging due to its complex relationships with macroeconomic variables and non-linear nature influenced by economic cycles.This study aims to enhance trade prediction accuracy by extracting common features from multiple variables to form economic cycle indicators. Using Taiwan's import and export data, along with related macroeconomic variables as predictors, we employ a novel approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for prediction.Our results demonstrate that the CNN-LSTM hybrid model outperforms other methods in predicting trade data with long-term memory characteristics, yielding lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Additionally, an LSTM model using input variables determined by economic theory shows impressive performance, indicating that integrating deep learning with economic theory can significantly improve model prediction accuracy.While factor models prove less effective than CNN, their simplicity and interpretability offer practical advantages. This research contributes to the field by showcasing the potential of combining advanced machine learning techniques with economic theory in forecasting international trade trends, particularly in the context of Taiwan's economy.

articleTitle: Using Physiological Signals for Pain Assessment: An Evaluation of Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Pain assessment is of major significance in clinical environments. The current gold standard is self-reporting of pain based on the patient’s subjective willingness. However, pain assessment based on physiological signals is developing rapidly due to the objectivity and real-time nature of physiological signals. This study aims to systematically compare the performance of convolutional neural networks (CNN) combined with long short-term memory networks (LSTM), bidirectional long short-term memory networks (BiLSTM), transformers, and gated recurrent units (GRU) models in pain classification tasks. We assessed these hybrid models’ performance experimentally using a variety of metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, training time, and inference time. The experimental results show that the CNN+Transformer model best performs in most evaluation metrics with an accuracy of 0.795, while the CNN+GRU model performs the worst with an accuracy of only 0.559. In addition, we also analyze the computational efficiency of each model in terms of training and inference time. Overall, this paper provides important direction for future research and real-world applications by thoroughly evaluating the effectiveness of various deep learning models in pain classification tasks.

articleTitle: Integrating Federated Machine Learning in Blockchain Crowdfunding Ecosystem for Increased Security and Transparency
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Crowdfunding has emerged as a popular and effective means of raising funds for various purposes, from business ventures and innovative projects to educational initiatives, healthcare facilities, and social causes. However, traditional crowdfunding systems face significant challenges due to inherent vulnerabilities that commonly lead to data breaches, compromising the personal and financial information of both investors and project creators. Developing and implementing a robust AI model in real-world environments is highly challenging, as many organizations are reluctant to share sensitive information with third parties, such as project creators, due to privacy concerns. Furthermore, creating a generalized prediction model is difficult because crowdfunding participants' data is fragmented across the ecosystem. To address these multifaceted challenges, this paper presents a novel approach that leverages the strengths of blockchain and AI technologies. Blockchain technology will ensure secure data access, while AI-based federated learning will be employed to develop a robust global model for real-time use.

articleTitle: Cost-Optimal Cutting and Packing for Nuclear Decommissioning
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: During nuclear decommissioning, large structures often need to be cut into smaller parts before being packed into containers. Cutting and packing incur costs, and improving efficiency in one often increases costs in the other, requiring a trade-off. Considering the operational costs of different cutting tools and container types, determining the optimal number of parts to cut a structure into, and how to pack these parts efficiently, is challenging. This paper presents a novel voxel-based cutting and packing optimization algorithm designed to minimize overall costs for decommissioning nuclear structures. We define cost as comprising two factors: cutting cost, which depends on the amount of cutting required and the type of tool used, and packing cost, which is determined by the number of containers needed and the unit cost of a container. We demonstrate that our algorithm can successfully minimize overall cutting and packing costs. Additionally, we show how our algorithm can be used to compare different decommissioning scenarios by cutting a simple structure found in nuclear decommissioning and packing the pieces into two different container types with different unit costs. Our results also show that the algorithm outperforms a minimal cutting approach, where a minimum number of cuts is used to segment the structure.

articleTitle: Traffic Motion Forecasting with Lightweight Network: A Novel Query Sub-Attention Branch-based Cross-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The advancement of autonomous driving requires improved scenario understanding and motion forecasting to ensure safer and more comfortable vehicle journeys. These components are essential for fully replacing human drivers and achieving highly automated driving. In uncertain traffic scenarios, autonomous driving software must anticipate critical situations and act with precision to ensure safety and comfort. Predicting the future trajectories of surrounding agents is vital for autonomous vehicles to operate safely. In this study, we introduce a novel sub-attention module and integrate it with the Cross-Attention mechanism to enhance contextualisation and improve the understanding of semantic relationships among distinct elements within the input sequence, named the Query Sub-Attention branch. Experiments were conducted to validate the proposed mechanism, which was integrated with the Dense-TNT model. The results suggest that the enhanced Cross-Attention mechanism enhances the traffic motion forecasting performance on the Argoverse 2 Motion Forecasting Dataset, showing promise as a generic module for integration with relevant models to advance autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-enhanced FBG Sensors for Human Body Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In order to study the change patterns of human body surface temperature under different movement conditions, which provides data reference for the intelligent development of rehabilitation robots, this paper designs a sensitized encapsulation structure of fiber Bragg grating (FBG) temperature sensor for body temperature measurement. This paper introduces the theory of FBG temperature sensing and proposes a sensitized structure using silica gel to encapsulate and copper shell to cover up, resulting in a sensor whose temperature sensitivity coefficient is increased to 119.3 pm/°C and temperature resolution reaches 0.008°C. Subsequently, the sensor was utilized on the human body to measure the change in body temperature in the process of " Sitting - Slow Walking - Sitting". It is found that the sensors can detect the change patterns of body temperature, which proves the feasibility of the sensor for body temperature monitoring.

articleTitle: Kinematic and Dynamic Analysis of the Cable Actuation in an Upper-Extremity Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Stroke is a medical emergency caused by a sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain, leading to brain cell damage. The symptoms of stroke vary in survivors, with most of them primarily suffer from a partial loss of motor ability. In this work, a lightweight cable-driven robotic exoskeleton with 3 DOFs, including abduction/adduction and flexion/extension of the shoulder joint, as well as flexion/extension of the elbow joint, was designed for the upper-extremity rehabilitation of stroke patients. To understand the variations in cable length during the operation of this exoskeleton, the kinematic characteristics of cable actuation were analyzed. Meanwhile, for the torque selection of applied motors, the dynamic characteristics of cable actuation were investigated. The analysis results serve as the foundation for position and force/torque control of this exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Design of the Control System and Geometric Parameter Error Calibration for a Rail-Based Cable Tunnel Inspection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: To address the need for manual intervention in the safety inspection of cables and associated equipment in underground cable tunnels, this paper presents the design of a control system for a previously developed five-degree-of-freedom rail-based cable tunnel inspection robot, achieving its motion control functions. A geometric parameter error model for the robot's onboard manipulator was constructed using the principle of differential transformation. Redundant parameters were eliminated through QR decomposition (Orthogonal decomposition), and the least squares method was employed to identify the geometric parameter errors of the robot. Finally, calibration experiments were conducted on the robot's geometric parameters, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed error model and compensation method, thereby providing a foundation for future research on the robot.

articleTitle: A Novel TBM Laser Target Angle Tracking System Based On Fuzzy Adaptive Sliding Mode Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The precision of TBM (Tunnel Boring Machine) guidance systems deteriorates under strong vibrations, and existing active vibration damping devices fail to ensure accurate angle tracking control between the guidance system and the TBM. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel angle tracking system for TBM laser targets, based on a fuzzy adaptive sliding mode control algorithm. The system utilizes six laser displacement sensors as sensing elements to establish a model for perceiving the relative motion state between the load platform and the base platform. By inversely solving the relative pose from the measurements of laser displacement sensors, a dataset is generated for training a neural network model. This model determines the relative pose directly from the sensor measurements. Additionally, a fuzzy adaptive sliding mode control algorithm has been developed. Using the relative pose as a feedback signal, this algorithm employs fuzzy rules to adapt to system disturbances and reduce the chattering in sliding mode control, achieving precise attitude tracking control between the load and base platforms. Simulation results demonstrate that the angle motion attenuation rates around the X, Y, and Z axes are less than 0.25 dB, 0.15 dB, and 0.01 dB, respectively, effectively tracking the angular motion of the base platform.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Task Offloading for Multi-User Distributed Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Edge Computing (EC) deploys multidimensional resources, including computation, storage, and communication, at the network edge to fulfill certain applications with stringent latency requirements. In the edge environment, computing tasks can be offloaded to mobile edge computing servers (MECS) for reduced task processing latency. However, traditional methods of task offloading in edge computing are inadequate for complex environments demanding high real-time performance. This paper focuses on studying the computational task processing problem in a multi-user distributed edge environment and propose a deep reinforcement learning-based multi-user distributed edge computing task offloading method aimed at minimizing task processing latency. The proposed method effectively addresses the computational task processing challenge in dynamic and complex edge environments with high real-time demands. Simulation results show that the proposed method has superior performance in terms of both task processing delay and algorithm execution time.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Framework for a Real-Time, Deep Learning Model to Estimate In vitro Chewing Cycles Required for Safe Swallowing
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Research on chewing robots is crucial for understanding and improving the mechanical process of food breakdown, helping to better replicate the human oral system. This study presents a novel conceptual framework for a machine vision and deep learning model that predicts the number of chewing cycles a robot needs to form a safe and swallowable bolus in real time, providing valuable insights into oral food breakdown. Utilizing image-based data acquisition and advanced deep learning algorithms, this model proposes a real-time in vitro chewing behavior analysis compared to existing robots. The methodology involves capturing chewing behavior through machine vision, data preprocessing, designing and training a deep learning model on time-invariant and time-variant variables, and optimizing for real-time predictions. The framework seeks to revolutionize the analysis of in vitro mastication processes, holding significant promise for various fields, including optimizing food product development, evaluating dental materials, and improving oral health products.

articleTitle: Degradation model of a system with compensation control strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The performance degradation of some key components is unavoidable in some electromechanical systems. To improve the system reliability and running quality, this work proposes a compensation control strategy for the key component according to the principle of the similarity between mechanical and other system, such as electrical systems. It is assumed that the degradation process of the key component follows Wiener process, and the explicit expression of the degradation model for the compensated system is an Ito process and obtained based on the model assumptions. According to the analysis results of the degradation model and numerical example, the proposed control strategy enables the key component to remain an output close to that of the new component before failure, and the gap between the new and compensated component is closely related to the parameters of the feedback loop. The results theoretically analyze the running principle of the compensation control strategy and provide theoretical support for further research on the reliability and maintenance modeling.

articleTitle: Design of an Eccentric Pole Type Magnetic Geared Composite motor
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: A novel magnetic geared composite motor is proposed based on magnetic field modulation, integrating multiple advantages of magnetic gears. To reduce axial size, a coaxial structure is adopted, embedding a permanent magnet synchronous motor inside the magnetic gear. To minimize torque ripple, a novel structure is designed: a high-speed inner rotor with eccentric magnetic poles is connected to a cup skeleton featuring radial magnetized poles on its inner and outer walls. The outer rotor employs a magnetic geared composite motor structure arranged in a Halbach array. The magnet modulation ring skeleton is 3D printed with PLA materials to reduce weight. To assess its effectiveness, finite element method is employed for electromagnetic simulation. The comparison with traditional magnetic geared composite motors which use various magnetization methods, indicates that the novel magnetic geared composite motor effectively reduces torque ripple and also demonstrates an improvement in output torque.

articleTitle: Environmental digital transformation capability, environmental organizational learning, and eco-innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Integrating digital transformation (DT) and sustainability transitions is a crucial issue and challenge for firms. There is limited research on how environmental digital transformation capability (EDTC) aligns with sustainability amid limited natural capital substitutability. This study illustrates how to integrate digital technologies and skills with environmental sustainability and further explores the roles of exploratory and exploitative learning within the context of environmental sustainability. It examines the relationship between EDTC, Environmental Organizational Learning (EOL), and eco-innovation in Taiwan's manufacturing industries. Focusing on firms undergoing digital transformations linked to Industry 4.0 and environmental sustainability, we gathered 310 effective samples. The structural equation modeling analysis confirms all direct effects and reveals that EDTC influences eco-innovation indirectly through both exploratory and exploitative EOL. These findings offer substantial academic and practical insights into sustainability under limited natural capital substitutability.

articleTitle: Fully 3D Printed Soft Electrostatic Loudspeaker
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Loudspeakers are essential components in human-machine interaction, enabling auditory communication between devices and users. However, most conventional loudspeakers are constructed from rigid materials, resulting in poor compliance and limiting their application in wearable technologies. In this paper, we introduce a novel soft loudspeaker fabricated using a customized 3D printer. This loudspeaker is made entirely of silicone rubber, which provides excellent compliance and biocompatibility, making it suitable for integration into wearable devices. The fabrication process involves the use of advanced multi-material 3D printing techniques to create a structure that can operate without the need for prestretch, enhancing its flexibility and ease of use. Experimental results demonstrate that the soft loudspeaker can produce satisfactory audio output when tested with real music input. The acoustic performance, including sound quality and volume, shows a close resemblance to traditional loudspeakers, while offering the added benefits of flexibility and comfort for the user.

articleTitle: Emotion Classification based on Multi Physiological Signals Using Hybrid Fusion Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The demand for emotion recognition is increasing not only in daily life but also in professional domains such as disease diagnosis and clinical rehabilitation. By monitoring non-invasive physiological signals of patients, providing timely feedback on their emotional state can significantly aid in patient recovery and subsequent expert treatment evaluation. In this study, we propose a mutual fusion approach utilizing both feature fusion and decision fusion techniques for emotion classification. Firstly, statistical knowledge-based methods were employed to select physiological signals and extract highly correlated and complementary features for feature-level fusion. Subsequently, a similarity weight, based on feature selection and statistical analysis, was incorporated into the decision fusion process. Our proposed method yielded promising results, achieving 82.5% accuracy and 75.2% macro f1 score for three-class classification (neutral vs. stress vs. amusement), 95.4% accuracy and 94.6% macro f1 score for two-class classification (stress vs. non-stress) using publicly available data from the WESAD dataset. These results demonstrate that employing a mutual fusion approach outperforms single fusion methods in emotion classification tasks.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a Parallel Mechanism Based Virtual Biomechanical Shoulder Robot Model
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The human shoulder complex provides an extensive spectrum of motion to the human upper arm, facilitating the accomplishment of the active daily life tasks. The in-silico musculoskeletal models presented in the literature can be used to study the associated kinematic parameters with the human shoulder. These models aid in the designing and control of rehabilitation robots. These models are sometimes oversimplified thus compromising their usage. This paper presents a Virtual 6-4 Parallel Biomechanical Shoulder Robot Model (VBSRM) as a musculoskeletal model. The kinematic model of the proposed VBSRM is developed. Performance metric such as condition number is identified to study the workspace of the VBSRM. A singularity analysis of the robot’s Jacobian matrix was carried out to avoid a possible singular design. In order to obtain the maximum workspace and optimal design of the VBSRM, design optimization was carried out using genetic algorithm. This proposed optimal design can be used in the shoulder functioning evaluations.

articleTitle: Differential Evolution-Based Universal Segment Preliminary Layout Method for Shield Tunneling
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The shield tunneling method is currently the most widely used underground construction technique, where the formed tunnel is composed of many sequentially arranged segments. Before construction, a preliminary layout of the design tunnel axis (DTA) is required to assess the segments' ability to fit the DTA and determine the number of segments needed. Existing preliminary layout methods only consider the axis fitting deviation of the next ring of segments to select the assembly point, which can lead to significantly increased axis deviations for subsequent segments, potentially exceeding allowable limits. This results in incorrect assessments of the segments' fitting ability, particularly for DTAs with small curvature radius. To address this issue, this paper proposes a segment preliminary layout method that considers the maximum fitting deviation of the next multiple rings of segments. The method uses a differential evolution algorithm to optimize the assembly point combinations of the next multiple segment rings. It employs a segment pose transfer algorithm to calculate the poses of the next multiple rings, and then computes the corresponding axis fitting deviations for these rings. The assembly point combinations with the minimum maximum axis fitting deviation is selected as the optimal solution, and the first assembly point is selected to assembly next segment. This method was applied to a 900m radius circular arc DTA using 28-point large diameter segments with a calculation of five segment rings. The maximum axis fitting deviation across the entire DTA was 9.3 mm, significantly lower than the 52.8 mm deviation obtained using existing layout methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing a Bellow-Structure Soft Actuator Simulations via a Novel Continuous Collision Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Accurate modeling of a soft robot remains a significant challenge in soft robotics. A precise model enables the more accurate control of the soft robot. Among various simulation methods, the finite element method (FEM) offers a more realistic representation of soft robot behavior. However, during simulations, soft robot bodies may experience collisions, especially with complicated structures, which results in challenges to traditional discrete collision detection. Collision detection is an algorithm that determines the limitations on the surface of the convolutions to avoid penetration. In this paper, a novel continuous collision detection algorithm is designed and proposed to benefit the accuracy performance of the FEM simulation during the contraction of a soft actuator, which contains a complex bellow structure with eight convolutions. The details of the algorithm are presented, along with initial validation results. The preliminary results demonstrate the potential of the proposed algorithm to enhance the accuracy of soft robot simulations. Further development and extensive algorithm validation are ongoing to contribute to the advancement of soft robotics modeling techniques.

articleTitle: Design of a Continuum Robot with Variable Stiffness Using Spherical Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Variable stiffness technology allows continuum robots to maintain flexibility while enhancing their load-bearing capacity. However, current technologies face issues such as limited stiffness variation and low torsional rigidity. This paper introduces a continuum robot with variable stiffness achieved through spherical jamming. The robot consists of multiple ball jamming joints, each formed by concentric, interlocking spherical friction layers. Inflating a thin-film airbag compresses these layers, locking the joint and altering the robot's stiffness. A cross-ball ring structure limits the joint's torsional freedom, providing high torsional stiffness. Experimental results show that the robot achieves up to 70 times variation in stiffness and retains a shear modulus of 3.4 MPa in its flexible state.

articleTitle: Kinematic Modeling and Control of a Continuum Robot in Confined Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: This study presents a continuum robot engineered for operation in confined spaces, including tasks such as the inspection and maintenance of specialized equipment and accessing the interior of aircraft wings. By applying the segmented constant curvature method, a refined kinematic control model is developed for the robot, and an integrated control framework is established. Extensive kinematic simulations have been performed to test the model, showing that it achieves reliable convergence with end-effector trajectory deviations consistently below 5 mm, reflecting a high degree of accuracy. This continuum robot stands out for its superior flexibility compared to traditional industrial robots and shows promising potential for diverse applications in complex and restricted environments.

articleTitle: Graph-Based SLAM for Under-Train Inspection Robots in Narrow Site
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Traditional Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) often fails when operating within narrow and repetitive metro train inspection pit environments. A novel SLAM framework is presented in this paper to address this problem. It integrates multi-sensor data and leverages prior knowledge of train structures, ensures consistent trajectory estimation in robot’s unidirectional straight runs up to 192m. By employing feature-based Laser Odometry (LO) and Time-of-Flight (ToF) ranging sensors for train wheel center detection, the SLAM frontend generates two types of keyframes. LO keyframes record timestamps, velocities, and pose estimations. ToF keyframes record timestamps when the ToF laser ranging point reaches the centers of the first and last wheels of each carriage. These heterogeneous keyframes are merged to serve as nodes in the factor graph. In addition to standard pose-to-pose constraints, the framework uses true distances between each carriage's first and last wheels, as well as estimated actual distances between carriages and from the robot's reached boundaries in the inspection pit to the centers of the first and last train wheels, as distance constraints between nodes. Finally, the backend optimization yields a globally consistent trajectory, an optimized feature map, and accurate center positions of each carriage’s first wheel in the inspection pit coordinate system. The proposed framework solves the issues of scale inconsistency in maps generated during real-time SLAM in each inspection session, as well as scale drift encountered during long-distance straight-line movements, ensures accuracy and safety in under-train inspections. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated using real-world datasets.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Knee Exoskeleton with Self-alignment Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The knee exoskeleton can assist patients for knee rehabilitation exercises. In this paper, a novel knee exoskeleton with self-alignment capability is proposed. First, the structure of the knee exoskeleton is designed, which has one active and four passive joints. The four passive joints are used to realize the self-alignment function of the knee exoskeleton. Second, the kinematic model is established and analysed. Third, simulations are conducted to validate the rotation ranges of human knee and hip joints. The simulation results demonstrate that the knee exoskeleton can meet the rehabilitation needs of the patients.

articleTitle: A Physics Informed Fusion CNN for Bearing Fault Diagnosis under Variable Rotation Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Rolling bearings are one of the key components in many mechanical equipment. Effective fault diagnosis of bearings is crucial for production safety and maintenance work. Despite variety of data driven fault diagnosis methods with high performance have been proposed, most of them learn fault features entirely from the training samples without the guide of physical knowledge, which leads to violation of physical laws and weak generalization ability. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a physics informed fusion convolutional neural network model for fault diagnosis of bearings under variable rotation speed. By embedding domain knowledge, the model’s accuracy and robustness are reinforced. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by comparative study under real data of fault bearings. The results show that the proposed model has a better interpretability and higher performance under high noise environments.

articleTitle: STRR-Net: A Swim-Transformer and Res2Net Architecture for Knee MR Images Multi-label Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a major cause of morbidity, especially in the older and female population. Automatic medical image segmentation is crucial for improving the diagnostic accuracy of KOA and optimizing treatment plans. Convolutional neural networks have evinced potential in enhancing the accuracy of KOA segmentation. However, CNNs face challenges in handling the complex variability in position, shape, and scale of segmentation targets. Additionally, existing CNN models struggle with accurate processing boundary information, which limits their effectiveness in clinical decision-making. To tackle these challenges, we introduce a deep-learning architecture known as STRR-Net, designed for the automated segmentation of knee joints in MRI scans. We also designed a novel parallel encoder structure to achieve complementary and enhanced feature extraction. In particular, we propose a skip-connection structure for multi-scale fusion, which allows us to simultaneously capture different levels of feature information. Our model attains an average Dice of 0.8176 for the knee dataset, with a score of 0.6653 for cartilage segmentation and 0.8320 for meniscus segmentation. Visualizing the feature maps allows for a detailed assessment of the knee joint’s anatomy, including cartilage thickness, thereby facilitating the timely identification of osteoarthritis.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor Fusion SLAM Algorithm Considering Wheel Slip
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: With the continuous development of automated guided vehicle (AGV) technology, simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has become a research hotspot. Currently, domestic AGVs mainly construct environmental maps based on laser radar scanning, while inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors and wheel odometry are used to provide attitude estimation and motion compensation, speed and displacement information respectively. However, when the drive wheels of the AGV slip, the wheel odometry can produce significant errors, leading to positioning errors and map drift. This paper uses an error state Kalman filter (ESKF) to fuse wheel-IMU odometry and a slip detection method based on slip rate. When the AGV slips, the wheel odometry data is promptly discarded, and the IMU pre-integration is used directly to replace the odometry, effectively reducing the impact of slipping. Through comparative experiments, it can be found that the algorithm can reduce the error caused by slip by about 78%, which has certain stability and accuracy, and can further improve the robustness of the system when applied to AGV.

articleTitle: Application of YOLO Algorithm in Monocular Visual Positioning of Cable Trench Inspection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence in the context of Industry 4.0. This study focuses on cable trenches and explores the application of monocular vision technology in cable recognition and localization in detection robots. The underground cable trench environment is complex and poses safety hazards. This study developed a cable recognition system using the YOLOv5 algorithm, which captures video images in real-time using a monocular camera. Combined with the camera's internal parameters, the system identifies and locates target objects. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves an efficient processing speed of 53.2 frames per second while achieving an average accuracy of 98.3%. Compared with actual measurement results, the effectiveness and accuracy of the algorithm in identifying target size and distance measurement have been verified.

articleTitle: An Image-Based Imitation Learning Framework for Robotic Writing Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Robotic writing, particularly in the realm of traditional Chinese calligraphy, poses unique challenges due to the intricate nature of stroke patterns and the high precision required. This paper presents an innovative image-based imitation learning framework designed to address these challenges by enabling robots to acquire and generalize writing skills from static images. By transforming static images into dynamic formats and incorporating a novel deviation analysis method, the framework enhances the learning of stroke thickness and allows for skill generalization across different writing scenarios. The proposed framework’s effectiveness is demonstrated through extensive simulations and real-world experiments.

articleTitle: System identification driven pre-filter design for dynamic compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Overshoot reduction is essential in high-precision control, and the designed pre-filters effectively mitigate this issue, leading to enhanced control accuracy and robustness, in particular when the closed-loop controller is not permitted to retuned by the users. This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic compensation through system identification-driven pre-filter design. By accurately modeling the closed-loop system’s dynamics, the proposed method enables the development of pre-filters that enhance system performance. The system identification process involves estimating the closed-loop system’s parameters using reference-output data, which are then used to design pre-filters compensating the specific dynamic characteristics. Experimental results from a drone demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed pre-filter design.

articleTitle: Language-guided visual attention network for visual grounding
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Visual grounding (VG) is a critical task that seeks to identify and localize a specific visual region within a given image based on a corresponding referring expression. Existing approaches to the visual grounding (VG) task can be categorized into three main types: two-stage methods, one-stage methods, and Transformer-based methods, which have achieved high performance. However, most of the methods do not exploit the visual and linguistic information well, limiting the performance of model. In this work, we propose a language-guided visual attention network for visual grounding, which can utilize language to deeply explore visual information by better processing of the relationship between vision and language. Specifically, we utilize BERT, a pre-trained model, to get the word-level and sentence-level linguistic features, which can understand the linguistic information more comprehensively. Inspired by the Transformer architecture, we design the stacked visual attention module, which leverages language to direct the attention of vision. In addition, we discuss several ways of fusing visual and linguistic features, enabling a better fusion of visual-linguistic information to obtain the correct coordinates. In a series of comprehensive evaluations on the ReferItGame benchmark dataset, our proposed model is shown to establish a new performance standard.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Control Strategy for Networked Vehicle Suspension Systems under Denial-of-Service Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The study of vehicle suspension systems is a critical component in ensuring enhanced comfort and stability for vehicles. In this paper, we propose an event-triggered control strategy for networked suspension systems to withstand denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. This strategy ensures vehicle driving stability and safety, while also minimizing the consumption of network resources. An attack-based Lyapunov function is used to obtain sufficient conditions with exponential stabilization and H∞ properties. Finally, the effectiveness of the controller is validated through system simulations conducted on a bumpy road.

articleTitle: An improved UNet with multi-field convolution residual module for turning tool wear segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In the CNC machining, the tool wear monitoring is a critical prerequisite for high-quality and high-precision machining. Traditional image segmentation algorithms rely too much on human expertise and are easily affected by environmental factors. This paper proposes an improved UNet model to achieve end-to-end high-precision segmentation of tool wear. The model introduces a multi-field convolution residual module. This module incorporates multiple 3*3 dilated convolution kernels to aggregate image features from different fields, and fuse image features from different fields through 1*1 convolution kernel. The module also adopts cross-channel residual connections by 1*1 convolution kernel to prevent the gradient vanishing. This improved UNet achieves a dice coefficient of 94.18% on a dataset of turning tool wear.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Moisture Content of In Vitro Chewed Food Boluses by Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the evaluation of moisture content in in vitro chewed food boluses using image processing techniques. This integration offers a novel, non-destructive method that enhances the accuracy and efficiency of moisture assessments compared to traditional gravimetric methods and external sensors, which are typically more time-consuming and potentially alter the sample's properties. Invitro food samples were taken for moisture analysis from a biomimetic robot equipped with automatic saliva injections. Image skewness, variance, lightness, and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) analysis were found to quantitatively indicate moisture content for two types of in vitro chewed food samples, at different chewing cycles and trajectories. This pilot study was conducted with two food samples, but the approach can be applied to a broader range. The study's findings highlight the effectiveness of image processing in analyzing moisture dynamics within chewed food boluses, providing valuable insights that could enhance the design and functionality of biomimetic chewing robots to resemble human oral processing more closely.

articleTitle: Damage Identification of Flexible PVC Substrate Based on VMD-ELM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: The substrate material of flexible antenna was easy to generate holes and cracks in the harsh airborne environment, Lamb wave test technology was proposed to detect the damage in the structure of flexible polyvinyl chloride (PVC) substrate and quantitatively reconstruct the damage shape to realize a nondestructive test. The damage identification method combined the variational mode decomposition (VMD) and extreme learning machine (ELM) pattern recognition. The VMD algorithm extracted the features of the echo signal without damage, hole and groove damage, constructs the damage feature vector, and ELM trains and tests to classify the damage types. There was a damage identification platform to set up for the damage detection of flexible PVC substrate. The results showed that the characteristics of low-frequency slowly varying echo signals were obvious after ELM processing; The ELM and BP neural networks trained and tested, respectively, and the damage types are classified. The ELM classification accuracy reached 91.67%. The ELM was better than the BP neural network method, which verified the effectiveness of the VMD-ELM algorithm combined to identify the damage characteristics of flexible PVC substrate. This method has a good application prospect in the rapid detection of early damage of flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: A Prosthetic Hand System with Human-Like Grasping by Combining EMG and Visual Information
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel prosthetic hand system integrated with a designed hybrid control method for achieving human-like grasping. The system design has been elaborated, including the mechanism design of a humanoid prosthetic hand equipped with multimodal sensing capabilities, a multi-channel EMG collector, a sensory feedback device, and a real-time central processing unit. A hybrid control method that combines electromyogram (EMG) and visual information was proposed to recognize the control intention of the system user. Preliminary verification of grasping experiments had been conducted, which proved the effectiveness of the prosthetic hand system and the hybrid control method. The development of this system aims to enhance the control performance and perceptual interaction capabilities of prosthetic hands while addressing limitations encountered in traditional myoelectric prosthetic hands. Besides, it could serve as a validation platform for assessing the control performance of diverse algorithms applied in practical applications.

articleTitle: Robot Agnostic Visual Servoing considering kinematic constraints enabled by a decoupled network trajectory planner structure
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: We propose a visual servoing method consisting of a detection network and a velocity trajectory planner. First, the detection network estimates the objects position and orientation in the image space. Furthermore, these are normalized and filtered. The direction and orientation is then the input to the trajectory planner, which considers the kinematic constrains of the used robotic system. This allows safe and stable control, since the kinematic boundary values are taken into account in planning. Also, by having direction estimation and velocity planner separated, the learning part of the method does not directly influence the control value. This also enables the transfer of the method to different robotic systems without retraining, therefore being robot agnostic. We evaluate our method on different visual servoing tasks with and without clutter on two different robotic systems. Our method achieved mean absolute position errors of < 0.5 mm and orientation errors of < 1°. Additionally, we transferred the method to a new system which differs in robot and camera, emphasizing robot agnostic capability of our method.

articleTitle: Feature Selection for Chip Defect Identification Using the Pied Kingfisher Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: In this study, we present the application of the Pied Kingfisher Optimizer (PKO) for feature selection in the classification of chip surface defects using Support Vector Machines (SVM). The dataset consists of images categorized into eight types of defects: center baseboard scratching, center baseboard scuffing, pin scratching, pin missing, pin scuffing, cracking, plastic baseboard scuffing, and melting. From these images, 27 features were extracted, including geometric properties, Hu moments, and GLCM texture features. The PKO was used to optimize the feature selection, significantly enhancing the SVM's classification performance. The accuracy is 94.2308%. The convergence curve, prediction comparison, and confusion matrix all indicated the effectiveness of the PKO in feature selection, leading to improved defect classification.

articleTitle: Tendon Drawn Pronation/Supination Actuation Concept for a Rigid Assistive Forearm Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: Pronation and supination of the forearm and wrist in the human body is permitted by a combination of movements from the carpal bones and the constrained relative motion between the radius and the ulna. Despite being crucial to completion of tasks involving the hand and arm, this degree of freedom is lesser explored with mobile and rigid exoskeleton designs for the upper limb. This paper presents the design, preliminary modelling, and prototype construction of a compact, robust, 1 degree of freedom rigid exoskeleton which circumvents these challenges by reframing a soft exoskeleton-based method of actuation - providing a structure on which to bear the forces created by the device, instead of transferring it through the body as a typical soft exoskeleton would. The design actuates wrist pronation/supination with tendons that directly power the motion through tension, actuating interlocking segments that progressively slide along each other in a cylindrical pattern. The exoskeleton essentially provides rigid support and utilises actuation principles of a soft robotics exoskeleton without suffering from the drawbacks. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Preliminary Study: Development of a Multi-Angle Posture and Scoliosis Assessment System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 30th International Conference on Mechatronics and Machine Vision in Practice (M2VIP)
abstract: With the influence of various factors, adolescents are facing increasingly severe posture problems, and the incidence of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is continuously rising. Traditional scoliosis assessment methods are labor-intensive, highly subjective, and pose radiation risks during treatment. Deep learning automated posture and scoliosis assessment have received increasing attention recently. However, most existing studies study single-perspective images and do not perform a comprehensive assessment using multi-perspective images. This paper proposed a system that can input multi-angle unclothed images of patients and calculate evaluation metrics based on landmarks to achieve a quantitative diagnosis. Currently, an experimental process for data collection has been established. In preliminary trials, the improved deep learning model achieved mAP of 62.9% in the back image, 62.4% inside body images, and 57.1% in the overhead images. In the future, as the amount of data increases, the overall capability of the system can improve further, allowing for better scoliosis assessment.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of a Wearable and Programmable Functional Electrical Stimulator Based on MCU
